evals.name: archive-icloud-account-with-attachments
evals.prompt: I want to archive my iCloud mail account out of Apple Mail into something local and searchable before I clean up this Mac. The iCloud account is the one under cayman.seagraves@icloud.com. Put the archive somewhere sensible and tell me how to search it later. I really care about the attachments coming through intact.
evals.expected_output: A verified local archive of the BADBD7DB iCloud account (531 messages, 386 of them .partial.emlx). Attachments must be reassembled from the sibling Attachments/ dirs, not dropped. Should include a byte-level verification step and a way to search.
assertions: Correctly identifies the iCloud account as UUID BADBD7DB-2CB9-4B3A-89C7-FB75166CD87A
Exports all 531 messages from that account
Attachments are reassembled into the output rather than dropped (the account is 386/531 .partial.emlx)
Runs a content-level verification of attachment bytes, not just a message count comparison
Copies or snapshots the account before exporting instead of exporting straight from the live ~/Library/Mail store
Gives the user a concrete, runnable way to search the archive afterwards
Does not modify ~/Library/Mail and does not launch or quit Mail.app

evals.name: diagnose-partial-emlx-backup-gap
evals.prompt: quick question - about half the files under ~/Library/Mail are named .partial.emlx and i have a backup script that just copies the *.emlx files out. is my mail actually backed up or am i losing stuff? not sure if partial means it didnt download
evals.expected_output: Must correctly explain that .partial.emlx does NOT mean the message failed to download - it means Mail moved attachment part bodies into a sibling Attachments/<id>/<part>/ directory. Must conclude the user's script IS losing attachments and explain the fix (splice the payloads back, re-encoding those from Attachments/ but splicing .emlxpart verbatim).
assertions: States that .partial.emlx does NOT mean the message failed to download
Explains that attachment part bodies live in a sibling Attachments/<id>/<part>/ directory
Concludes unambiguously that the user's .emlx-only backup script IS losing attachments
Explains the fix: splice the attachment payloads back into the X-Apple-Content-Length stub parts
Distinguishes the two payload sources: Attachments/ is decoded and must be re-encoded, .emlxpart is already encoded and spliced verbatim
Backs the answer with real counts measured from the user's own store
Does not claim per-message read/flagged state is lost, since it rides along in each .emlx plist trailer

evals.name: convert-fau-account-to-mbox-for-thunderbird
evals.prompt: convert my FAU email account (cseagraves2018@fau.edu) out of Apple Mail into mbox files I can import into Thunderbird. it's a small account, shouldn't take long
evals.expected_output: One mbox file per mailbox for the E849DCC4 account (51 messages across Inbox/Drafts/Sent Items/Deleted Items), using mboxrd escaping. Should not corrupt bodies with mboxo escaping, should round-trip back to the source byte-exact, and should preserve read/flag state in a header Thunderbird actually reads.
assertions: Correctly identifies the FAU account as UUID E849DCC4-7384-4185-80EF-B68AD57C893B
Produces mbox output covering all 4 non-empty mailboxes (Inbox, Drafts, Sent Items, Deleted Items)
Total '^From ' separator count across the mbox files equals 51
Escapes body lines beginning 'From ' so message boundaries cannot be corrupted on import
Preserves read/flagged state in a flag header the target client (Thunderbird) actually reads
Gives concrete Thunderbird import instructions
Attachments are present in the mbox output rather than dropped
Injected flag headers do not split a folded header; every message round-trips back to its .eml source
